message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to refuse to back up when someone else drove the wrong way into an ATM lane. Let me break this down step by step. First, the setup: My bank has an ATM that's a drive-up. It's in a small cutout with clear arrows pointing to the entrance. Since it's a drive-up, the ATM is on the left side where the driver sits. That makes sense because in most places, drivers sit on the left. But the problem is, it's easy for people to turn the wrong way into this cutout. That's exactly what happened today. I arrived at the bank, took the turn to go into the ATM area, and another car whipped in the wrong way. Their passenger was using the ATM. I was in a hurry because I needed to get to class, so I was annoyed. The person took 15 minutes, fumbling with their cards, inserting and reinserting them multiple times. I waited patiently but was getting more annoyed each minute. When she finally finished, she leaned out the window and yelled at me to move. I didn't respond because no one was behind me, and I was already late. I didn't move. After about five minutes of her shouting, she did a K-turn and left. I told my friend about this, and he said I was being a dick for not just backing up since no one was behind me. But I still think I was right to stay because they were going against traffic. So, is it right or wrong for me to refuse to move? Let me think about the rules. In most places, you're supposed to follow traffic signs and arrows. The ATM area has clear arrows, so going the wrong way is against the rules. That person was breaking the rules by entering the wrong way. But she was using the ATM, so maybe she thought it was okay. On the other hand, I was already there, waiting to use the ATM. She cut in front of me the wrong way, which is not fair. She was causing a blockage because she was in the wrong lane. I was in the correct position, so I think I had the right to stay. But my friend says I should have just backed up because no one was behind me. That makes sense in terms of being polite, but I feel like I was in the right legally. I also consider the safety aspect. If I had backed up, would that have been safe? Since no one was behind me, it might have been okay. But she was already in the wrong lane, so maybe she should have been the one to back up. It's a bit confusing. Another angle: the ATM area is designed for one-way traffic. By entering the wrong way, she was creating a potential hazard. If I had moved, I would have been following her, which is against the traffic flow. So, staying put was safer for everyone. But then, being polite and accommodating might have been the better choice, even if it's against the rules. It's a bit of a dilemma between following the rules and being courteous. I also think about the time I was wasting. She took 15 minutes, which is a long time for an ATM. She was causing a delay for me, and then she was yelling at me. That's not a good way to behave either. Maybe she was stressed, but that's no excuse for cutting in the wrong way. In the end, I feel like I was in the right because I was following the traffic rules, and she was not. But my friend thinks I should have been more accommodating. I guess it's a matter of perspective. I prioritize following the rules and safety, while he prioritizes being polite and not causing a scene. So, after all this, I think it's right for me to refuse to back up because she was going against traffic. But I can see why someone might think I was being stubborn or rude. It's a tough call, but I stand by my decision.
